solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A select tug is at sea avoiding second wave, say

indicators.note: at sea means jumbled, and avoiding says one letter of that jumble goes unused

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for a second of time

explanation.surface: A tugboat crew is out on the water, dodging a second big wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' scrambles A SELECT TUG IS, and 'avoiding second' then removes one S from those twelve letters. 'wave, say' marks waving as just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave your arms is one example of making expressive movements with the hands and arms.

clue.text: Good lecturer in work with experts gets to travel widely

indicators.note: in places the lecturer's letter inside the following pair of words

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
aces are experts or top performers
L stands for lecturer, as in university abbreviations

explanation.surface: A capable academic who works alongside experts gets to see the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes travelling far and wide, though it usually also means becoming successful.

clue.text: Recommend group just outside medal positions reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a set is a group of things; fourth place comes just after gold, silver and bronze

explanation.surface: A selection panel recommends a squad that finished just short of the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: SET plus FOURTH sounds the same as the answer, which swaps the number for 'forth'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth a proposal is to put it forward or propose it, close to recommending it.

clue.text: Elected eastern European when broadcast is sound

definitions.note: a sound is a narrow stretch of water, a noun here

parts.note: a party that is elected is in, in power

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian, from the Baltic states

explanation.surface: An elected Latvian makes a sound point when his speech goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when broadcast' turns LETT, a Latvian, into its sound-alike LET. 'sound' is the geographical noun, not noise or soundness.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow channel of sea water, much like a small bay or creek.

clue.text: Divert attention from a guest agitated about parking

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumble wraps the next letter
agitated means stirred up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A guest, flustered about where to park, draws everyone's attention away from the hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' jumbles A GUEST into USTAGE, and 'about' puts it around P.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage, an actor who moves upstage forces others to turn away from the audience, stealing their limelight.

clue.text: Frenchman amid apprehension getting physical support?

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: apprehension of a suspect is their arrest
M is short for Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman being arrested gets some bodily help as he's taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' places M inside ARREST. The question mark admits the definition is playful: the support is for a physical arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair's side rest literally supports part of the body, a pun on bodily support.

clue.text: Work of agents to promote say a top model, nothing less

indicators.note: in a down entry, promoting raises things upward, so the pieces read bottom to top

parts.note: EG (for example) is what 'say' means
top means number one, written NO I

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to model is to pose
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A talent scout pushes a supermodel to the top, holding nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' drops O from POSE to leave PSE. 'to promote' reverses EG + A + NOI + PSE, reading upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the business carried out by secret agents.

clue.text: Soft element in massage

definitions.note: soft here is a noun-like sense, a softy or fool; Chambers gives fool for both

indicators.note: an element in a word is a part of it, so the answer lies inside

explanation.surface: A soothing touch is one component of a good massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft' is the British sense of simple or foolish, used for a silly person, not gentle pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can describe a fool: someone soft in the head is a donkey-like idiot.

clue.text: Bird in a cove fluttering close to boat

indicators.note: fluttering suggests restless movement, so these letters are mixed
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bird flits about a little bay near a moored boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' jumbles A COVE into AVOCE; 'close to' gives the final T of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Period in day associated with crashing?

definitions.text: Period in day associated with crashing?

parts.words: Period in day associated with crashing?
parts.note: crashing is slang for falling asleep, and a midday nap is when people crash out

explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' suggests accidents, but it is slang for dozing off.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon nap in hot countries is a regular time of day for sleeping.

clue.text: Colourful growth in first of peonies and others

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A gardener admires bright blooms among the leading peonies and other flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower's coloured leaf-like part grows from the bloom, a vivid outgrowth of the plant.

clue.text: Spare home for demolition in army communication?

indicators.note: a building marked for demolition will be broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spare house is earmarked for knocking down to make room for the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for demolition' scrambles SPARE HOME. 'army' is a pun: flag signalling is done with the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag signalling uses arm positions to send messages, so it is quite literally communication by arm.

clue.text: A fight with mug requiring shift in attitude

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A brawl that ends with someone punched in the face makes him change his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of opinion or policy, from the military command to turn round.

clue.text: Old Green in Strasbourg easily seen?

parts.note: vert is French for green, and Strasbourg is a French city

explanation.surface: An old Green politician is clearly visible in the European Parliament at Strasbourg.
explanation.walkthrough: Strasbourg tells you to translate into French. 'Old Green' looks like a veteran environmentalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is open and unconcealed, plainly visible to all.

clue.text: Style and energy shown by northern aristocrat

definitions.note: a verb here: to style someone is to give them a name

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
an aristocrat holds a title, used loosely here for the titled person

explanation.surface: A northern lord shows panache and vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' is the verb meaning to name or address someone formally, not flair.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone a Duke is to give them that designation or title.

clue.text: Students might face this peer in sporting contest

parts.note: students sit tests, an exam they must face
a peer is an equal, a match for someone

explanation.surface: A student could find themself up against a classmate in a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' suggests a lord, but here means an equal. The answer is an international cricket fixture lasting up to five days.
explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket or rugby game between national teams is a sporting fixture.

clue.text: Danger that's hidden in stall for greyhounds

definitions.meaning: a concealed snare or pitfall that catches the unwary
in greyhound racing the dogs start from boxes called by this name

explanation.surface: A hidden hazard lurks in the starting box at the dog track.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a snare is a concealed danger, and greyhounds race from starting boxes known by that name.

clue.text: Prosper and show off

definitions.meaning: to wave something about ostentatiously, brandishing it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to thrive and to brandish something flamboyantly.

clue.text: Operation to accept mobile phones in non-unionised place

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
mobile means moving freely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business operation agrees to take mobile phones in a workplace with no union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' is the anagram signal and 'to accept' the container. Strictly, the term means a workplace where union membership is optional rather than banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A workplace that employs staff regardless of union membership, the opposite of a closed one.

clue.text: First principle book put out is unchanged

indicators.note: put out means removed, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a basis is a foundation, a first principle

explanation.surface: The founding principle in the book has been left exactly as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' deletes the B of book from BASIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold in its current state, without alteration, as used of second-hand goods.

clue.text: Activity successful with long breaks?

parts.note: in this cue sport a break is a run of consecutive pots, and long ones win frames

explanation.walkthrough: 'long breaks' reads like holidays, but in cue sports a break is a scoring sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The cue game played on a large table rewards players who make long scoring breaks.

clue.text: Coincide somewhat with couch potato's eating preference?

definitions.meaning: to extend partly over something, sharing some ground
a sofa-bound viewer eats with the plate above their knees, not at a table

explanation.surface: A sofa-loving viewer's habit of eating on their knees partly matches someone else's.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: food held above the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: When two things partly share the same space or time, one extends partially across the other.

clue.text: Get too old for striking and argument about wages essentially

parts.note: workers on strike are out

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre letter

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Strikers in a pay dispute decide they are past this sort of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the central G of wages, and 'about' wraps ROW around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To become too big or mature for something, as a child does with clothes or toys.

clue.text: Who in Provence meets cook without fine flan?

parts.note: qui is French for who, and Provence is in France

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a chef is a cook
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone in Provence meets a chef who has no fine tart to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without fine' drops F from CHEF, leaving CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury egg custard tart in pastry is a classic type of open tart.

clue.text: Rule arising about date sounded harsh

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the Raj was British rule in India
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A regulation coming up about a deadline grated on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RAJ upward to give JAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise that grated or clashed unpleasantly on the ear is said to have done this.

clue.text: Remove weapons from one French Arab male

parts.note: un is French for one
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and an Arab man take away someone's guns.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or formal synonym for disarming someone, stripping them of arms.

clue.text: Truth none grappled with at a critical point

indicators.note: grappling means wrestling, so these letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody had wrestled with the truth at the crucial moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grappled with' scrambles TRUTH NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something at the moment of changing, such as milk just going sour.

clue.text: Record business reduced by 50%

indicators.note: halving the word means losing its second half

parts.note: an enterprise is a business

explanation.surface: A firm's books show business has halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by 50%' cuts ENTERPRISE in half, dropping PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it in a ledger or log.

clue.text: About to sit again with Republican having temporary control?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the answer's use as in an interim government

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
to retake an exam is to sit it again

explanation.surface: A Republican is about to re-sit an exam while briefly in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works as an adjective, as in a stand-in government before an election.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim government or manager holds power only until a permanent replacement is chosen.

clue.text: Tourist's first nervy in place with quads?

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word

parts.note: high means keyed up and jittery, as nervy is

explanation.surface: A jittery tourist is staying somewhere with college courtyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quads' suggests Oxford college quadrangles or quadruplets, but here means quadriceps.
explanation.definitionFit: The quadriceps muscles sit at the front of the upper leg.

clue.text: Destroy odd piece among umpteen deliveries

indicators.note: an odd piece lying among the words points to a fragment concealed in them

explanation.surface: A cricketer wrecks the occasional ball among countless deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd piece' also defines the answer (as in odds and ends), so the clue doubles as a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to finish it off, kill it or destroy it.

clue.text: Man on prior show excited adulation

parts.note: he stands for a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man at a monastery's prior show is thrilled by the praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' looks like the head of a priory, and 'excited' its mood, but 'excited' signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Extravagant admiration of someone, treating them as an idol.
